A live drawing layer, leaves that collide with lettering, and a bear controlled by a state machine.

Play with the bear ↗Renderer & interaction source ↗Simulation source ↗
01

The interaction

The idea came from wanting to feed little creatures letters from the website. The page uses notebook ruling, pencil strokes, and an autumn tree drawn directly in Canvas.

The creatures and scenery are original drawings made from paths in code.

02

Creature state machine

A bear idles until it finds an unclaimed letter. It approaches that letter, eats when it is within reach, then celebrates with a flip. After three letters, it can produce a cub. The population is capped at four.

idle→seek→eat→flip→idle / cub

Each letter belongs to at most one bear. That reservation stops several bears trying to eat the same character. The “Inspect” control draws those targets and collision bounds over the scene.

03

Fixed-step simulation

Letters fall under gravity, bounce off the ground, and collide with one another. Their positions update in fixed steps, independently of how often the screen redraws. Walking and flipping are drawn procedurally from the current behavior.

Pointer coordinates are converted into the simulation’s own coordinate system, so dragging also works as the scene changes size. Keyboard users can activate a name letter or use the feed button.

accumulator += elapsed;
while (accumulator >= 1 / 120) {
  world.step(1 / 120);
  accumulator -= 1 / 120;
}
render(world);
04

Drawing and leaf physics

A seeded branching algorithm constructs the autumn tree. The opening traces those branches progressively, then releases leaves. Each leaf has position, velocity, rotation, and a falling or resting state.

The page measures the name letters and section headings in document coordinates. Swept collision detection catches leaves crossing the top of a letter between simulation steps. A resting leaf stays attached to its letter until wind dislodges it or the letter is fed to a bear.

Pointer motion and scrolling contribute to a damped wind field. The margin vines reveal with reading progress. The simulation uses fixed time steps, a bounded leaf count, and stops when the tab is hidden.

Drawing & interaction source ↗Leaf simulation source ↗
05

Motion controls

The opening drawing plays on each homepage load, with Skip and Replay controls. Reduced-motion preferences skip the opening and start the motion paused. The simulation stops updating offscreen and while the tab is hidden. Eaten heading letters return, and a reset clears the habitat.

The site’s source is public. This website and its browser demonstrations were developed with AI assistance; the supplied Python project is available separately in its original form.
